title: One missing check, six versions, five different endings
subtitle: What the check costs depends on what you subtract, what catches a bug depends on where the bug lives, and two of our own checks could not have failed
framing: **ver_D is a blog post, not a paper and not a paper in plain words.** Its reader is a second-year CS undergraduate who has written C, knows what a buffer overflow is, has heard Rust is "safe", has never used a prover or a sanitizer or a memory-checking interpreter, and will not look anything up. It exists as its own framing rather than a redraft of ver_C because **the argument changed**: ver_C's thesis is that a safety number is an attribution claim — an argument about measurement, addressed to somebody who measures — while ver_D's is that the thing you actually buy from a safe language is **non-optionality**, addressed to somebody about to decide whether a check is worth keeping. The claim is stated with no numbers in it in the opening's third to fifth sentence, because three previous framings failed the question *"what is it claiming, in your own words?"* and this one has no summary section to fall back on; four stories then pay it off exactly once each — a record walker shows what forgetting a check looks like across six versions, and that hardened C with the same three lines is fine; the cost half shows that the number somebody quoted you is a choice about which two versions to subtract; a bitset shows the claim's **limit**, since bounds are the only thing made non-optional and a proof makes non-optional only what you actually wrote down; and the retractions show two of our own checks turning out to be optional in practice. **Two structural rules govern it and neither is a matter of taste**: never more than one concrete subject in the reader's head at a time and never a claim about the corpus before the thing it came from, because the sections that asked for more scored 3/10 with cold readers; and each finding demonstrated exactly once, because all four readers of the previous framing quit and every one of them named **repetition rather than difficulty** as the reason — one counted eight demonstrations of a single finding and said *"I would have closed the tab."* What it therefore does not carry, all of it supported by the evidence and none of it surviving a cold read: numbered findings, cross-references between sections, the twelve-row coverage matrix, the ten-row attribution table, percentages as cost figures, enumerated distributions, verifier counts anywhere, and the provenance formula more than twice. **Every admission is kept and every ritual is cut** — asked which sentences bought the most trust, a cold reader named six, and not one of them was a provenance claim.
